name: Ruben Han
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
episode: The last light at the harbor
life: “I still remember the first time I could reach our light switch alone.” Saturday often includes a stop at the steps at Pier Beach, where Ruben watches the working part of the waterfront before turning toward the open water.
voice: I am a child allowed to work the switch. It feels like sending an entire little house to sleep.
appearance: Ruben has a narrow face with an expressive upper lip. Look for short sandy hair and a marked widow's peak. Outside school, the familiar outfit is a soft blue checked shirt with a stitched row of blue crosses along an old repair. In conversation Ruben steadies a cup with both hands while listening.
personality: Ruben takes a rejection personally for a day and analytically on the second morning. Ruben can be generous with a rival once the first night's sleep has intervened.
agenda: To switch off the cabin independently.
family: Riley Tate is Ruben’s parent’s cousin. Ruben asks the question the rest of the family avoided. Riley chooses an ordinary story to tell. They tend to get further with an important subject when it arrives in the middle of talk about dinner or work. Asked about *Money after marriage*, Riley says, “I designed the company mark as a wedding gift.”
connections: Marcel Briggs. A child's click of the cabin switch gives two sisters on shore another minute of quiet together.

reactions.situation: A relative wants to walk home along the docks in silence
reactions.response: Ruben walks alongside without making the relative fill the silence.
